subject: Open vs Proprietary Concordance: governance, acceptance thresholds & next steps
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@concordfinance.com>, Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@concordfinance.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-06-18T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Open vs Proprietary Concordance: governance, acceptance thresholds & next steps

Hi Samir / Aisha —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and the items we agreed to own from Redwood's side. I kept this intentionally tight so we can move to a short pilot quickly.

What we heard from Concord
- Primary goal: move invoice categorization model off a proprietary vendor to an open model to reduce unit cost by ~3x while matching current label accuracy and hallucination tolerances.
- Acceptance constraints: precision on vendor labels must not drop more than 3 points; conjunction errors (mis-labelling vendor/address as line-item) must be <= 2% of tokens.
- Compliance: models must be deployable in private VPC; audit logs + KMS required.

Redwood proposed next steps
1) Pilot scope: 10k invoice samples run through 2 open candidates + your current baseline for parity assessment. (Owner: Redwood / Priyom)
2) Benchmarking metrics: overall accuracy, per-label precision/recall, hallucination rate (defined below), latency P95, cost/token. Parity pass if accuracy within 0.03 of baseline AND hallucination rate <= baseline + 0.015. (Owner: Concord + Redwood)
3) Prompt set & acceptance harness: we will deliver a vetted prompt bundle + unit tests for common failure modes. (Attachment: prompt-bundle-concord-v1.zip)
4) Governance playbook: proposed rollout gates (sprint-based, canary percentages, auto-fallback to baseline model). (Attachment: mutual-action-plan-Concord.docx)

Immediate asks from Concord
- Provide a sample of 10k anonymized invoices (PII masked) and a single-person contact for data transfer + SOC questions.
- Confirm NDA addendum to allow model-output-based metrics to be shared across teams.

Benchmarks and where to look
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_ConcordBenchmarks (I uploaded the initial metric template and the prompt bundle.)
- HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DEAL-8742 (I linked the sprint plan draft.)

We'll start the pilot once we have data and the NDA tweak. Priyom and Vivek will own model selection and the acceptance gate definitions. Marcus will scope infra for a Dedicated pilot in your us-east region.

Thanks —
Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Subject: Re: Open vs Proprietary Concordance: governance, acceptance thresholds & next steps

Lauren —

Appreciate the concise plan. A few clarifications from our side:
- The 3-point precision headroom is a hard constraint for our compliance team. If open models can't meet that in pilot, we need a documented mitigation (e.g., tighter prompting + post-filter).
- Hallucination definition: we mean any generated token that introduces a new, incorrect vendor/payment entity not present in original invoice data. Your threshold looks reasonable.
- Data share: we'll get you 10k masked invoices by 06/24. Contact for transfer is Aisha (cc'd).

Question: are there recommended open candidates you'd like us to prioritize shipping with the dataset? Also would you share the prompt set examples you plan to test?

Thanks —
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Data Science, Concord Finance
samir.patel@concordfinance.com
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodai.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@concordfinance.com>, Aisha Gomez <aisha.gomez@concordfinance.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodai.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-06-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Open vs Proprietary Concordance: governance, acceptance thresholds & next steps

Hi Samir / Aisha —

Quick technical note on recommended candidates and acceptance checks before the pilot:

Recommended open model candidates (initial shortlist)
- OpenCandidate-A (Llama-3-70B-FT, q4f16): best throughput vs sensitivity tradeoff on our internal invoice shards.
- OpenCandidate-B (Mistral-65B-ax): typically better at structured extraction with minimal prompt engineering but slightly higher cost per token.
- Distilled option for latency tests: Llama-3-13B-quant (to measure canary latency behavior).

Acceptance metrics (concrete)
- Baseline accuracy (proprietary): 0.872 overall accuracy (we will verify after you upload labels).
- Open parity gates: overall_accuracy >= 0.842 OR delta_accuracy >= -0.03 (whichever is stricter).
- Per-label floor: no label falls below baseline by more than 0.04.
- Hallucination rate: measured as % of invoices with at least one hallucinated entity. Gate: <= baseline + 0.015.
- Latency: for canary 95th percentile must be <= 850ms end-to-end for the 13B distilled candidate; larger models can be allowed higher P95 but must meet throughput targets.

Benchmark procedure
1) Run 2-shot and zero-shot prompt variants from the prompt bundle across the 10k set (we'll attach the exact harness).
2) Evaluate structured extraction outputs against your gold labels using the metric template.
3) Add a blackbox regression test that flags samples with hallucinated entities (we'll provide heuristics).

Prompt examples are attached in prompt-bundle-concord-v1.zip (file contains 12 prompts + negative-case prompts). We'll push an updated prompt with a structured JSON schema enforcement to the Drive by EOD.

I'll kick off lab runs as soon as we have the dataset accessible. If the open candidates clear the parity gates, we can discuss a phased migration plan: 20% canary -> 50% -> full. If they don't, we will document recommended mitigations and fallback policy.

Cheers —
Priyom
Senior ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwoodai.com

Date: 2027-06-20T10:32:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Open vs Proprietary Concordance: governance, acceptance thresholds & next steps

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Samir.

Action items and owners (short list)
- Concord: deliver 10k masked invoices + baseline labels by 2027-06-24 (Owner: Aisha).
- Redwood: upload structured comparison harness & schema enforcement prompt to Drive and kick off first-run by 2027-06-25 (Owner: Priyom).
- Redwood Infra: provision a small Dedicated pilot pool in us-east with KMS + VPC routing; estimate cost and share by 2027-06-22 (Owner: Marcus).
- Governance doc: draft rollback & canary thresholds; share PR to the mutual-action-plan document by 2027-06-23 (Owner: Lauren).

Risks called out
- If per-label drops exceed 4 points on high-value vendor labels we will not proceed to canary — need explicit acceptance from Concord security/compliance.
- If hallucination heuristics flag >3% of invoices on the open model, we will apply a post-filter stage in the pilot and re-evaluate.

I'll set up a 30-min sync for 06/26 to review pilot outputs (calendar invite to follow). Thanks everyone — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Lauren
